rv.q: Her movement here is inventive and frequently thrilling, especially in unison, but can't maintain the initial level of quivering intensity, the middle section becoming a series of mournful vignettes.
The Surge shares with Sinéad O'Connor a refusal to be limited by expectations and a determination to tackle unexpected themes making it a worthy celebration of a challenging and inspiring artist.
The choreography matches the mood of the songs, danced with skill and commitment by this experienced cast.
Joyce Theater’s dull dance tribute to Sinéad O’Connor misses the singer’s transcendence
The Surge is not a perfect show. But Sinéad O'Connor was never interested in perfection. She was interested in truth. And that, emphatically, is what this is. Absolutely unmissable.
The Surge is both a battle cry and a sanctuary for women who have something to say, whether or not the world is ready to listen.
Sonya Tayeh has created a fitting tribute while delivering a production that stands confidently on its own.
I don't think that I have ever before seen a cast move with such harmony, community and solidarity.

cn.t: Critics praise Sonya Tayeh's powerful tribute to Sinéad O'Connor, with ten women dancers over 40 delivering a visceral, devotional performance that captures the singer's uncompromising spirit through bold contemporary choreography and her iconic music.
